headline: Microsoft's Azure cloud division is reported to have been told to find at least 20% in cost savings as AI data-centre spending rises, which Microsoft disputes.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: read in full with Microsoft's denial; a single report from unnamed sources, so the score does not rise.
importance_line: What changed is a report that Microsoft's cloud chiefs are looking at cutting at least a fifth of costs to pay for AI data centres, which matters first to the roughly 11,500 people in the Azure software division and to outside contractors, then to cloud customers such as OpenAI that depend on Azure, then to Microsoft's shareholders, and the doubt is that it rests on unnamed sources and Microsoft denies it.
summary: The Information reports, as relayed by Stocktwits on Yahoo Finance and citing people familiar with the matter, that Girish Bablani, president of Azure's software development group, told leaders in his roughly 11,500-person division to outline ways to cut expenses by at least 20%, to help offset heavy spending on AI data centres and pay higher salaries to keep staff from rivals such as Meta and Anthropic. A Microsoft spokesperson disputed this, saying "Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans." The exact measures are not settled and could include parting with outside contractors, the report did not say whether job cuts could follow, and the pressure comes although Azure's revenue grew 40% to $101.9 billion in the 12 months to June.
notes: Read the Stocktwits account of The Information's report on Yahoo Finance; The Information's own page was not opened. Microsoft disputes the report, so the status is DISPUTED.
